methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Standard Subsea is a seed-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by Christopher Amidon that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws on a private comparables universe of three frontier-tech peers in the same sector (Clippership, NetworkOcean, and Albacore); no public company benchmarks are available for direct comparison.

The stage-progression method was applied as the primary valuation framework. Using total capital raised ($10M) as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, the method implies a post-money valuation of $25M. This represents standard step-up dynamics observed in frontier maritime tech companies moving through funding rounds.

The triangulation analysis, constrained by limited methodological inputs, supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, with a central estimate of $25M. The relatively narrow band reflects reliance on a single applicable method; the low and high bounds incorporate modest variance around the core multiplier assumption. Key uncertainties center on whether the $10M+ raised figure represents all capital to date, the degree to which private peers' recent funding rounds reflect current market sentiment in subsea technology, and the absence of public market reference points. Additional data on revenue trajectory, burn rate, and peer-specific transaction multiples would narrow this range materially.
